title: Container Bookings: No-Show History and New Booking Requests
content:
In Container Bookings a customer's no-show record is judged over its whole portfolio of bookings, and that record can close a product to new requests.

## Policy clause

The no-show count of a customer is the number of no-show fees entered on any of that customer's bookings with a booking date falling in the trailing window of 90 calendar days that ends on the date of the new request, both ends included. A no-show fee that was afterwards waived as goodwill still counts, because the no-show itself took place. A new booking request for a given product may be accepted only while this count is below the no-show threshold of that product. Once the count has reached the threshold of the product requested, the request is declined for that product and no charge of any kind arises. The customer remains free to request any product whose threshold the count has not reached, subject to the ordinary admission rules for booking requests. A cancellation, a declined request and a roll made by the carrier are never counted as a no-show.

## Evidence and correlation

The count is taken from the line's charge records, not from the customer's own account of its history. It is assembled across every booking of the requesting customer and is established before the request is answered.

## The window in plain terms

The window consists of the request date together with the 89 calendar days immediately preceding it. A no-show fee dated on the first of those days is inside; one dated the day before that is outside.

## Decision table

| No-show count compared with the product's threshold | Outcome for a request for that product |
|---|---|
| Count lower than the threshold | This rule does not stand in the way |
| Count equal to the threshold | Declined, without charge |
| Count higher than the threshold | Declined, without charge |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- A product with a threshold of 3, and a customer whose count is 2: this rule permits the request.
- The same product, and a customer whose count is 3: the request is declined for that product, while a product whose threshold is higher than 3 would still be open under this rule.
- A customer with one no-show fee that was later waived and one cancelled booking: the count is 1, since the waived fee counts and the cancellation does not.

The thresholds and histories in these cases are illustrative inputs.
